summary: npm/jsDelivr abused as CDN for browser redirect payload; no installer-side harm
details: px.js is a browser-only script (references document/window) that injects a full-viewport iframe pointing at an external domain (mfmz.tfnbgh.cn/H.html). A bundled maintainer script update_px8my.sh rotates that destination domain, bumps the package version, runs npm publish, and purges jsDelivr caches — the package is being used as a mutable redirect endpoint delivered through jsDelivr's npm mirror. The package.json declares no preinstall/install/postinstall lifecycle hooks; require()/import in Node fails because the code depends on browser globals. Installing this package as an npm dependency does not execute the redirect payload, exfiltrate installer data, fetch remote code, or otherwise harm the installing machine. The victims of the redirect behavior are end-users of websites that embed the jsDelivr URL (a browser-side scam/affiliate-cloaking concern), which is outside this engine's installer-harm threat model.
